newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan compares U.S. aid to cost of embassy move.
newsitem.headline: Jordan compares U.S. aid to cost of embassy move.

text.p: Crown Prince Hassan of Jordan has said promises of an additional $100 million in U.S. aid to his country have been tarnished by a controversial congressional vote on moving the U.S. embassy in Israel to Jerusalem.

Jordanian newspapers on Tuesday quoted the crown prince, who is in Washington to conclude the aid package with President Bill Clinton, as saying that Washington allocated as much money to moving the embassy as it had to Jordan's aid increase.

"It is coincidental that $100 million is almost equivalent to the sum total of the aid package promised to Jordan, which of course will not go down well at home," the Jordan Times quoted the prince as telling an audience of U.S. officials, ambassadors, and Middle East experts.

The congressional vote, reaffirming Congress' view that Jerusalem should remain Israel's undivided capital, was bitterly criticised by Palestinians and their Arab allies, who saw it as further evidence of Washington's pro-Israel bias.
Israel captured Arab East Jerusalem 30 years ago from Jordan and later annexed the eastern part of the city. Palestinians regard it as the capital of a future Palestinian state.
Jordan's extra $100 million in aid is expected to be funded by $50 million cuts in Washington's big annual aid packages to Israel and Egypt.
Israel, which receives $3 billion in U.S. civilian and military aid each year, is the largest recipient of U.S. aid. Egypt's $2.1 billion aid package is second only to Israel's.

Israeli officials have portrayed the aid transfer to Jordan as a gift from Israel, but the Jordan Times quoted a Jordanian official as saying the extra cash "was American money -- an American concern".
Jordan received $47 million in U.S. civilian and military aid this year and Clinton has asked for $75.6 million for 1998.
Since signing a peace treaty with Israel in 1994 and distancing itself from neighbouring Iraq, Jordan has also won debt forgiveness and military assistance worth around $1 billion.
